# Install Paneflow on macOS

> Install Paneflow on an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 13 Ventura or later. Choose Homebrew or the DMG, verify the installation, and set up terminal access.

Canonical: https://paneflow.dev/docs/installation/macos

<!-- Auto-generated mirror of paneflow.dev - do not edit by hand.
     Source of truth: the paneflow.dev docs. Regenerated by
     scripts/sync-public-docs.ts in the site repo. -->

Paneflow requires **macOS 13 Ventura or later** on an **Apple Silicon**
Mac. Use Homebrew if you already have it installed, or download the
`.dmg` for a manual installation. Both methods install the signed and
notarized `PaneFlow.app`. You do not need Rust or build tools.

## How do I install Paneflow with Homebrew?

Open Terminal and install the Paneflow cask:

```bash
brew install --cask arthjean/paneflow/paneflow
```

Homebrew installs `PaneFlow.app` in `/Applications` by default. If the
`brew` command is not found, use the DMG instructions below. You can also
use the DMG if Homebrew does not yet offer a newly published release.

## How do I install Paneflow from a DMG?

Open the [latest Paneflow release on GitHub](https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases/latest),
or run this command to open the release page in your browser:

```bash
open https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/releases/latest
```

1. Download the file named `paneflow-<version>-aarch64-apple-darwin.dmg`.
   `<version>` is the release number shown on the page.
2. Open the downloaded `.dmg` in Finder.
3. Drag `PaneFlow.app` onto the `Applications` shortcut in the disk image.
4. Wait for the copy to finish, then eject the disk image.

## Open Paneflow

Open `PaneFlow.app` from Applications, or use Spotlight (`Cmd+Space`,
then type `PaneFlow`). You can also launch it from Terminal:

```bash
open -a PaneFlow
```

If macOS asks you to confirm opening an app downloaded from the internet,
choose **Open** for the copy you just installed. For other alerts, follow
the Gatekeeper instructions below.

## How do I verify the installation?

Run the installed executable directly:

```bash
/Applications/PaneFlow.app/Contents/MacOS/paneflow --version
```

The command should print the installed version. Check that the app also
opens. If the file is not found, check that `PaneFlow.app` is in
`/Applications`, or repeat the installation.

Then use the [getting started guide](/docs) to launch your first agent.
Install CLI agents separately and follow their sign-in instructions.

## Use the paneflow command in your terminal

Installing the app does not automatically add its executable to your
shell's `PATH`. Try `paneflow --version` first. If it prints the installed
version, skip this section.

Otherwise, create a symlink to the installed executable. These commands
create `/usr/local/bin` if needed and preserve any existing `paneflow` entry:

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/bin
sudo ln -s /Applications/PaneFlow.app/Contents/MacOS/paneflow /usr/local/bin/paneflow
/usr/local/bin/paneflow --version
```

If `ln` reports `File exists`, check the entry with
`ls -l /usr/local/bin/paneflow`. If it already points to the installed app,
skip the link command. If it points elsewhere, use the full app path
shown in the verification section.

If the full path works but `paneflow` is not found, add `/usr/local/bin`
to your shell's `PATH`. In Bash or Zsh, run `export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$PATH"`
and try `paneflow --version` again. To keep the setting in new terminals,
add the same export line to `~/.zshrc` for Zsh or `~/.bash_profile` for
Bash login shells.

## What if macOS blocks PaneFlow.app?

The official DMG is signed and notarized. If macOS reports an unverified
developer, first download a fresh copy from the release page above.
If you have verified its source and it remains blocked, follow
[Apple's instructions for opening a blocked app](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102445):

1. Try opening `PaneFlow.app` once.
2. Open **System Settings**, then **Privacy & Security**.
3. Find the notice for `PaneFlow.app` and select **Open Anyway**.
4. Confirm **Open** in the next dialog.

If the option is unavailable on a managed Mac, contact your administrator.
If macOS reports that the app is damaged or will harm your computer,
keep it blocked and [report the installation problem on
GitHub](https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/issues), including the exact
alert, your macOS version, and the Paneflow version.

## What about Intel Macs?

Paneflow does not publish an Intel macOS build. The Apple Silicon DMG
cannot run on an Intel Mac. The [Linux installation guide](/docs/installation/linux)
and [Windows installation guide](/docs/installation/windows) describe the
builds and processors supported on those operating systems.
